ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

payload.proof_nl:
Work in the formal power series ring Z[[q]]. Since 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, all indices occurring in the q-Pochhammer symbols are nonnegative, so the definitions make sense.

First rewrite the rational function R_{a,b,r}(q). Because a <= b, we have
(q;q)_{r+b}/(q;q)_{r+a} = (\prod_{t=1}^{r+b} (1-q^t))/(\prod_{t=1}^{r+a} (1-q^t)) = \prod_{t=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1-q^t).
Reindexing with t = r+i gives
(q;q)_{r+b}/(q;q)_{r+a} = \prod_{i=a+1}^{b} (1-q^{r+i}).
Also,
(q;q)_a/(q;q)_b = (\prod_{t=1}^{a} (1-q^t))/(\prod_{t=1}^{b} (1-q^t)) = 1/\prod_{t=a+1}^{b} (1-q^t).
Therefore
R_{a,b,r}(q) = \prod_{i=a+1}^{b} \frac{1-q^{r+i}}{1-q^i}.
When a=b, these are empty products and equal 1, so the same formula is still valid.

Now fix an integer i >= 1. In Z[[q]] one has
(1-q^i) \sum_{m>=0} q^{mi} = \sum_{m>=0} q^{mi} - \sum_{m>=0} q^{(m+1)i} = 1,
because the coefficient of q^0 is 1 and for every positive multiple ni of i the two sums contribute equally and cancel. Hence
(1-q^i)^{-1} = \sum_{m>=0} q^{mi}
inside Z[[q]].

Substituting this inverse into the product formula for R_{a,b,r}(q), and using that the product over i is finite, we obtain in Z[[q]]:
R_{a,b,r}(q) = \prod_{i=a+1}^{b} (1-q^{r+i})(1-q^i)^{-1}
= \prod_{i=a+1}^{b} \left((1-q^{r+i}) \sum_{m>=0} q^{mi}\right)
= F_{a,b,r}(q).
Thus F_{a,b,r}(q) is exactly the formal power-series expansion at q=0 of the rational function R_{a,b,r}(q).

For the final claim, assume R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q]. A polynomial, viewed as an element of Z[[q]], is equal to its own power-series expansion at q=0 (with all coefficients above its degree equal to 0). Since the expansion of R_{a,b,r}(q) is F_{a,b,r}(q), we have equality of formal power series
R_{a,b,r}(q) = F_{a,b,r}(q)
in Z[[q]]. Therefore, for every integer j >= 0, the coefficients of q^j are equal:
[q^j] R_{a,b,r}(q) = [q^j] F_{a,b,r}(q).
This proves the lemma.
payload.role_in_assembly: Replaces the polynomial coefficient problem for R_{a,b,r} by the corresponding formal-series coefficient problem for the interval product F_{a,b,r}.

payload.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define (q;q)_0 := 1 and (q;q)_n := product_{t=1}^n (1 - q^t) for n >= 1. Define the rational function R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b). Also define the formal power series F_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+i)) * sum_{m>=0} q^(m i)). Then F_{a,b,r}(q) is the power-series expansion at q = 0 of the rational function R_{a,b,r}(q). In particular, if R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q], then for every integer j >= 0 one has [q^j] R_{a,b,r}(q) = [q^j] F_{a,b,r}(q).

detailed_findings.finding: The product rewrite R_{a,b,r}(q) = \prod_{i=a+1}^b (1-q^{r+i})/(1-q^i) is correct, including the empty-product case a=b.
The justification that (1-q^i)^{-1} = \sum_{m\ge 0} q^{mi} in Z[[q]] is valid coefficientwise in the formal power series ring.
The final coefficient comparison under the assumption R_{a,b,r}(q) \in Z[q] is complete and matches the lemma's 'in particular' clause.

result_payload.reason: The proof matches the lemma statement closely and is mathematically complete. It correctly rewrites the q-Pochhammer quotient as the finite interval product, identifies each factor (1 - q^i)^{-1} with the geometric series sum_{m>=0} q^{mi} in Z[[q]], and concludes that the finite product F_{a,b,r}(q) is exactly the formal power-series expansion of R_{a,b,r}(q). Under the additional assumption R_{a,b,r}(q) \in Z[q], the coefficient identity follows immediately from equality in Z[[q]]. No undeclared or forbidden dependencies are used.
